# L-91451 — The positive physical two-ledger cone is generated by the pure equality and reserve rays

Claim ID: `L-91451`  
Status: **PROVED EXACT TWO-RAY CONE / GEOMETRIC CHILD THEOREM**  
Created: 2026-08-12  
Depends on: `L-91108`, `L-91339`, `R-91450`  
RH status: **unproved**

## 1. Physical target and score map

For a positive physical state

\[
 (L,R)\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2,
\]

define its SHARP target and endpoint score by

\[
 T=L+2R,
 \qquad
 S=2L+R.
\tag{L-91451.1}
\]

The inverse map is

\[
\boxed{
 L=\frac{2S-T}{3},
 \qquad
 R=\frac{2T-S}{3}.
}
\tag{L-91451.2}
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
 (T,S)\text{ comes from a positive }(L,R)
 \iff
 \frac12T\le S\le2T.
}
\tag{L-91451.3}
\]

The boundary rays are the pure reserve state `(L,R)=(0,R)`, with `S=T/2`,
and the pure equality state `(L,R)=(L,0)`, with `S=2T`.

## 2. Relation to the common-kernel cone

The common positive measure of `L-91339` imposes the stronger constraint

\[
 S\ge\frac54T
\]

by `R-91450`. Thus

\[
 \boxed{
 \text{common positive kernel cone}
 \subsetneq
 \text{positive physical two-ray cone}.
 }
\tag{L-91451.4}
\]

The witness at `x=5` lies in the physical cone but outside the common-measure
cone. This explains why target subordination is required when one insists on a
single score-exact positive measure.

## 3. Pure-channel kernel realization

Retain the positive source atoms

\[
 w_2(x,n)=\frac{2\sqrt x}{n}-\frac1{\sqrt n},
 \qquad
 w_1(x,n)=\frac{\sqrt x}{n}-\frac1{\sqrt n}.
\]

For positive measures `nu_L,nu_R`, define

\[
 L_x=\sum_n\nu_L(n)w_2(x,n),
 \qquad
 R_x=\sum_n\nu_R(n)w_1(x,n).
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
 T_x=L_x+2R_x,
 \qquad
 S_x=2L_x+R_x
}
\tag{L-91451.5}
\]

lies in the full physical cone. Conversely, every scalar pair in that cone has
such a two-ray realization, already using one atom in each channel.

This is a scalar source-typing theorem. Exact divisor and row typing still
requires the resident Hall/component maps.

## 4. Coefficient-one geometric child in each ray

Let `p` be prime and `r=p^-1/2`. For `a in {1,2}` and `n<=x/p`,

\[
\boxed{
 w_a(x,n)
 =w_a(x/p,n)
  +a(1-r)\frac{\sqrt x}{n}.
}
\tag{L-91451.6}
\]

For `x/p<n<=x`, the parent atom is a positive activation frontier. Thus each
pure physical ray separately has:

```text
one coefficient-one canonical child at x/p;
one positive harmonic slack;
one positive activation frontier.
```

The two-ray physical cone is invariant under this geometric source split.

## 5. Score orientation firewall

The two rays do not have the same local score surplus:

```text
pure equality slack:  score = 2 * target;
pure reserve slack:   score = target / 2.
```

Therefore arbitrary independent two-ray measures do not automatically give a
nonpositive score loss. The coupled common-measure construction of
`L-91339/L-91340` is stronger precisely because its equality and reserve parts
combine to produce the positive surplus

\[
 W_S-W_\Psi=\frac{\sqrt x}{n}>0.
\]

Hence `L-91451` enlarges the admissible source cone but does not replace the
score-exact/target-subordinate Hall construction.
